question: Can frozen representations of self-supervised neural dynamics models reveal physical observables and laws through a fixed linear readout, and do fine-tuning or high-capacity downstream probes instead create apparent competence or destroy the latent physical structure being evaluated?

key_findings.claim: PhyIP is a three-stage, frozen-backbone protocol: fit one time-invariant linear readout on in-distribution activations, evaluate it zero-shot on parameter-shifted simulations, and symbolically regress the probe outputs into a candidate physical formula.
key_findings.evidence: The backbone m_theta remains fixed while W,b are trained by supervised regression from h(t) to s(t+1). Fluid models use a local 1x1 convolution followed by global summation; PySR then searches simple formulas and the resulting formula is tested on OOD regimes. Raw-input, time-dependent, MLP, last-layer-tuning, and full-fine-tuning baselines vary measurement capacity or invasiveness.

anchors.section: Feature Extraction, Linear Probing, and Equation Discovery

key_findings.claim: The strongest fluid results occur for UNetConvNext on the 2D turbulent layer and 3D red-supergiant tasks, where the frozen probe reaches correlations 0.83 and 0.91 and symbolic regression returns pressure-based energy expressions.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 reports TRL-2D MAPE 36.9+/-1.2%, rho 0.83+/-0.02, SSL OOD error 0.20+/-0.01 and E approximately 1.48P. For RSG-3D it reports MAPE 18.2+/-0.9%, rho 0.91+/-0.01, SSL error 0.02+/-0.00 and E approximately 1.45P+0.42 rho v_r^2. These are OOD summaries over 9 cooling rates and 3 stellar phases, respectively.

key_findings.claim: The 3D supernova is an explicit negative result for the frozen probe and symbolic discovery, while task-supervised full fine-tuning looks much better and is interpreted as learning the diagnostic task rather than exposing SSL knowledge.
key_findings.evidence: All four SSL backbones have high OOD error (0.30-0.40) and PhyIP correlations no higher than 0.21; UNetConvNext has MAPE 140.4% and rho 0.15. Symbolic regression returns the unphysical inverse-pressure expression E approximately 0.35-0.06/(P+0.2). Full FT reaches MAPE 18.3+/-18.5% and rho 0.71+/-0.01 despite the failed frozen readout, whereas raw input, time-dependent, MLP, and LL-FT obtain 142.1/0.22, 93.2/0.64, 125.5/0.48, and 65.0/0.59 (MAPE/rho).

key_findings.claim: Low SSL prediction error is not sufficient for linear accessibility in the reported table, contrary to the paper's broad low-error-to-linear-decoding narrative.
key_findings.evidence: On RSG-3D, FNO and TFNO have low SSL OOD errors of 0.05 and 0.04 but only rho 0.22 and 0.25 with MAPE 95.1% and 92.5%; UNetClassic has the worse SSL error 0.09 yet rho 0.69 and MAPE 25.6%. Thus architecture/latent placement strongly mediates probe success even at low predictive error, and the claimed implication is not established empirically.

key_findings.claim: The TRL raw-input control is internally anomalous: the stated target is exactly linear in an input channel, yet the reported linear raw-input baseline performs poorly.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix C defines the TRL input as including pressure P and the target as E_int=integral P/(gamma-1)dV with fixed gamma=5/3. A linear map over flattened P can therefore compute the target exactly up to fixed voxel-volume scaling, but Table 1 reports MAPE 58.5% and rho 0.32 for 'Linear Probe on Raw Inputs.' No preprocessing, constraint, or implementation detail is supplied that reconciles this failed positive control.

anchors.section: Table 1 / Linear Probe on Raw Inputs

key_findings.claim: On the synthetic two-body benchmark, the selected frozen block-9 probe decisively beats full fine-tuning OOD, but a time-dependent probe and frozen MLP are numerically at least as strong.
key_findings.evidence: Across 50 OOD test sets, PhyIP reports MAPE 24.5+/-4.2% and rho 0.91+/-0.02 versus full FT/IBP 81.5+/-12.4% and rho 0.05+/-0.35. The time-dependent probe is 12.1+/-1.2% and 0.96, and the MLP probe is 22.5+/-3.0% and 0.88; raw input and LL-FT are 65.2/0.45 and 45.3/0.65.

key_findings.claim: The orbital headline result is optimistically selected on its evaluation set: block 9 was chosen by sweeping layers on the same 50 OOD test sets used for the reported 0.91 correlation.
key_findings.evidence: The authors explicitly state that blocks.9 was selected 'via a systematic analysis per block on the 50 OOD test set'; Figure 4 peaks at that block. There is no nested validation set or corrected layer-sweep comparison, so both the chosen representation and its final OOD score use the same data.

key_findings.claim: Fine-tuning is associated with deep-block parameter change, low CKA, and reduced single-neuron correlations to dynamic variables, but these diagnostics do not by themselves establish targeted erasure or its causal direction.
key_findings.evidence: Blocks 5-10 show roughly 10% relative parameter change and CKA below 0.2; among the top 20% most-modified MLP neurons, maximum correlations with speed/radius fall about 0.15 while mass is stable. This is compatible with representational distortion, but CKA change can reflect reparameterization, information could move to other neurons, and the analysis conditions on the most-changed neurons without a preservation or rescue intervention.

key_findings.claim: The manifold pictures cannot support direct geometric-collapse comparison because PaCMAP is fitted independently to the frozen and fine-tuned activation sets.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix D states Z_ssl=PaCMAP(h_ssl) and Z_ft=PaCMAP(h_ft) are obtained by independent fits. Independent nonlinear projections have unrelated coordinate systems and can alter global layouts, so Figure 3 can show within-panel color organization but cannot make the two 2D shapes a commensurate measure of geometric destruction.

anchors.section: Figure 3: The Failure of Invasive Probing

key_findings.claim: Symbolic regression recovers a visible inverse-square term but not the complete Newtonian force law, and the appendix is more qualified than the main text.
key_findings.evidence: Ground truth is proportional to m1*m2/r^2. The selected rank-3 PhyIP formula is approximately 0.1/r^2+sin(...), omitting both masses and retaining an unspecified residual; rank 1 is 1/(1/r+1.16), and rank 2 is nested sine. The main text's notation P(r,m2)+1/r^2 and statement that the residual 'vanishes' are not quantified by held-out formula error. The result supports recovery of distance scaling, not the full law.

key_findings.claim: The solar-system appendix preserves important PhyIP failures and calibration problems that temper the paper's general robustness language.
key_findings.evidence: Venus falls to rho about 0.4 with MAPE above 50%; Uranus retains rho about 0.8 but MAPE about 70%; the plotted Neptune correlation is also around 0.4. The invasive probe is worse, including about -0.9 correlation on Jupiter, but the later statement that the non-invasive probe remains above 0.85 on 'these same planets' is not true across the displayed planetary suite.

key_findings.claim: The claimed probe-error bound is a heuristic derivation rather than a proved consequence of SSL error, and it targets a different quantity than the implemented probe.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix assumes g(0)=0 and writes g(h)=Jh+R_g, but then replaces E||g(h)-Delta x||^2<=epsilon with E||Jh-Delta x||^2 approximately epsilon without bounding R_g, decoder curvature, or the distance of h from zero. It also labels W*=mu_Phi^T J 'optimal' without a covariance-based least-squares argument. Equations 4 and 19 bound prediction of Delta s=s(t+1)-s(t), whereas Equations 5-6 and the experiments train W h+b to predict the level s(t+1).

anchors.section: Equation 4 and Why a Linear Probe for Physics

key_findings.claim: Appendix setup details conflict with each other on fluid spatial resolution, weakening reproducibility.
key_findings.evidence: Sections C.1-C.3 specify TRL-2D as 128x128 and both RSG-3D and SN-3D as 64^3. Table 3 instead lists 384x128 for TRL and 256x128x256 for RSG while retaining 64^3 for SN. The paper does not explain whether these are native-grid versus cropped/resampled model resolutions.

method.core_idea: Treat a pretrained dynamics network as a fixed measuring instrument: extract a chosen hidden activation, fit the lowest-capacity time-invariant linear map that can recover a physical observable, require generalization to unseen physical parameters, and only then distill the readout into a symbolic candidate law.
method.mechanism: For residual next-state prediction x_hat(t+1)=x(t)+g(h(t)), the authors argue that a low-error decoder makes h locally consistent with the physical update. A fixed linear probe is intended to average the local gradients of a smooth physical functional Phi, while a time-dependent or nonlinear probe can fit local curvature itself. In experiments, ridge regression or a 1x1 convolution plus summation reads frozen features; PySR searches formulas; fine-tuning controls test whether supervised adaptation changes the backbone and OOD behavior.
assumptions: The dynamics are autonomous and Lipschitz, the physical functional Phi is C2-smooth, and its gradient has finite Lipschitz constant K_Phi.
The predictor is residual with an origin-preserving decoder g(0)=0, and activations lie close enough to the null-latent expansion point for g(h) to be approximated by one fixed Jacobian J.
Small SSL next-state MSE implies small error of the decoder's linear term Jh, although the appendix does not bound the nonlinear remainder needed for this implication.
A physical quantity that is linearly decodable from frozen activations and generalizes across selected parameter shifts is treated as evidence of latent physical structure.
One time-invariant readout is the relevant capacity restriction; time-dependent readouts are treated as capable of solving local curvature rather than measuring a representation.
The selected activation site is representative of the model; in the orbital experiment this site is chosen by a sweep over the OOD test sets.
Supervised probe training data are in-distribution and separate from SSL pretraining, while the reported OOD simulations use unseen cooling rates, phases, environment variables, or orbital systems.
The observable labels are valid tests of learned dynamics even when they are deterministic or near-deterministic functions of input state channels, such as TRL energy from pressure.
Pearson correlation and MAPE summarize physical recovery adequately despite calibration sensitivity, near-zero denominators, unclear aggregation units, and no hypothesis tests.
Symbolic formulas selected from a constrained PySR search and evaluated on the designated OOD data reflect the probe's latent law rather than feature leakage or formula-selection overfit.

Fine-tuning on the narrow diagnostic distribution is representative enough to support claims about invasive adaptation generally, although the paper does not test representative adaptation or linear-probe-then-fine-tune controls.

techniques.role: Restricts the diagnostic to a fixed affine readout so the backbone cannot change and the readout cannot rotate with time.
Maps each spatial latent vector to a local energy contribution with a 1x1 convolution and sums over the physical domain.
Tests probes on unseen cooling rates, stellar phases, supernova environments, and orbital systems.
Compares raw linear, fixed latent linear, time-dependent linear, frozen MLP, last-layer tuning, and full tuning.
Uses PySR to turn probe predictions into compact pressure-, velocity-, or radius-dependent expressions.
Measures linear and nonlinear probe performance across transformer blocks, though selection and reporting reuse the OOD set.
Measures similarity between frozen and fine-tuned representations across layers.
Localizes relative Frobenius-norm weight changes to attention and MLP modules in deep blocks.
Checks whether neurons with large weight changes lose correlation with speed, radius, force, mass, or momentum.
Plots each activation set in two dimensions; useful within panels but not a shared-coordinate comparison.

evaluations.setting: TRL-2D, 9 unseen cooling rates; UNetConvNext frozen bottleneck probe.
evaluations.metric: OOD internal-energy MAPE, Pearson rho, and SSL OOD next-state error.
evaluations.result: 36.9+/-1.2% MAPE, rho 0.83+/-0.02, epsilon 0.20+/-0.01; SR gives E approximately 1.48P.

evaluations.metric: OOD energy MAPE and Pearson rho.
evaluations.result: Raw input 58.5%/0.32; time-dependent 22.1%/0.88; frozen MLP 37.2%/0.72; LL-FT 32.5%/0.80; full FT 41.2%/0.81.
evaluations.baseline: Fixed PhyIP UNetConvNext 36.9%/0.83; the raw-input result conflicts with the exactly linear pressure target.

evaluations.setting: RSG-3D, 3 unseen stellar-evolution phases; UNetConvNext frozen probe.
evaluations.metric: OOD internal-energy MAPE, Pearson rho, and SSL error.
evaluations.result: 18.2+/-0.9% MAPE, rho 0.91+/-0.01, epsilon 0.02+/-0.00; SR gives E approximately 1.45P+0.42 rho v_r^2.

evaluations.setting: SN-3D, 27 unseen ambient-density/metallicity environments across four backbones.
evaluations.metric: OOD internal-energy MAPE, Pearson rho, and SSL error.
evaluations.result: PhyIP fails: MAPE 92.1-140.4%, rho 0.08-0.21, epsilon 0.30-0.40; SR gives an unphysical inverse-pressure formula.
evaluations.baseline: Full FT 18.3+/-18.5% and rho 0.71+/-0.01, showing diagnostic-task learning despite failed frozen decoding.

evaluations.setting: 109M-parameter orbital transformer, 50 synthetic OOD force-vector tests; block-9 readout.
Layer sweep on the same 50 orbital OOD test sets.
evaluations.metric: Probe Pearson rho and MAPE by transformer block.
evaluations.result: Linear rho rises from about 0.3 at block 1 to about 0.91 at blocks 6-9, with MAPE falling from about 0.7 to 0.25; block 9 is selected.
evaluations.baseline: MLP is stronger in early blocks and roughly tied in deep blocks; selection is not evaluated on a fresh set.

evaluations.metric: Relative parameter change and linear CKA.
evaluations.result: Deep blocks 5-10 show approximately 10% changes and CKA below 0.2, while early blocks remain near CKA 1.
evaluations.baseline: Early blocks 0-4 have less than 2% parameter change.

evaluations.setting: Top 20% most-modified MLP neurons in the orbital transformer.
evaluations.metric: Change in maximum absolute neuron-variable Pearson correlation.
evaluations.result: Speed and radius decodability drops roughly 0.15, with a larger local momentum drop, while mass changes little.
evaluations.baseline: Static-variable correlations; no all-neuron information or causal rescue baseline is reported.

evaluations.setting: PySR on orbital probe outputs, 7 candidate equations selected on a complexity/MSE Pareto frontier.
evaluations.result: The selected PhyIP rank-3 expression contains 0.1/r^2 plus a sine residual; lower ranks do not recover 1/r^2.
evaluations.baseline: Ground truth m1*m2/r^2; invasive FT uses nested sine and distorted radius/mass decay.

evaluations.setting: Solar-system OOD suite from Mercury through Neptune.
evaluations.metric: Force-vector Pearson rho and magnitude MAPE.
evaluations.result: PhyIP is strong on several planets but falls to about rho 0.4/MAPE >50% on Venus, rho 0.8/MAPE about 70% on Uranus, and roughly rho 0.4 on Neptune.
evaluations.baseline: Fine-tuning is broadly worse and reaches roughly rho -0.9 on Jupiter.

evaluations.setting: Appendix theoretical diagnostic for a C2 physical functional and residual decoder.
evaluations.metric: Claimed expected squared error of a fixed linear probe for Delta s.
evaluations.result: Claimed upper bound C1 epsilon+C2 K_Phi^2 Var(x)+O(Delta t^4).
evaluations.baseline: The derivation does not control the decoder Taylor remainder and the experiment predicts s(t+1), so this is not a validated bound for the implementation.

limitations: Author-stated: a fixed linear probe cannot recover highly nonlinear, entangled encodings; future work should explore subspace-constrained or weight-preserving adaptation that protects already encoded invariants.

Reviewer-identified: the theoretical bridge from SSL error to linear probe error is incomplete because g(h)-Delta x being small does not imply Jh-Delta x is small without a bound on the decoder remainder, latent radius, or decoder Hessian.

Reviewer-identified: the theory bounds the update Delta s, while the implemented probes predict the level s(t+1); a shortcut through state retention can therefore satisfy the experiment without the claimed update geometry.

Reviewer-identified: TRL's target is an exact linear function of input pressure, so probe success may measure preservation of an input sufficient statistic rather than discovery of a physical law; the inexplicably weak raw-input positive control is unresolved.

Reviewer-identified: low SSL error is not sufficient in Table 1—RSG FNO/TFNO predict well but decode poorly—so the result is architecture- and layer-dependent rather than the claimed general implication.
Reviewer-identified: block 9 is selected and evaluated on the same 50 OOD sets, introducing model-selection leakage into the central orbital score.
Reviewer-identified: most reported means and +/- values lack definitions of replicate unit, seed count, confidence interval, or significance testing; RSG has only three OOD phases.
Reviewer-identified: independently fitted PaCMAP projections do not provide a shared geometry, and CKA/weight drift establish change rather than loss of all task-relevant information.

Reviewer-identified: the neuron-erasure analysis conditions on the most-modified neurons and checks maximum marginal correlations; it neither tests redistribution to other neurons/subspaces nor rescues performance causally.

Reviewer-identified: fine-tuning uses a deliberately narrow diagnostic distribution, including a single star mass. The results show corruption under that setup, not that adaptation is intrinsically destructive; representative fine-tuning and LP-FT are absent.

Reviewer-identified: the recovered orbital formula contains only a partial 1/r^2 term, omits the mass product, retains a sine residual, and has no reported held-out symbolic-model error or stability across PySR runs.

Reviewer-identified: high frozen-probe correlation is correlational evidence of accessibility, not proof that the SSL model uses the decoded quantity causally for next-state prediction; no activation intervention is performed.

Reviewer-identified: Appendix C and Table 3 disagree on TRL and RSG resolution, and the paper supplies optimizer summaries but no code or complete preprocessing/aggregation specification in the reviewed version.
failure_modes: A probe can decode a state variable already present in the inputs without the model representing the governing transition law.
A linearly inaccessible but causally used nonlinear code produces a false negative, as the authors acknowledge for entangled representations.
A high-capacity probe or fine-tuned network can learn the target from supervised labels and produce a false positive about pretrained knowledge.
Layer or hyperparameter selection on OOD test data inflates apparent generalization and makes cross-method comparisons optimistic.
Narrow diagnostic distributions remove variation in mass, force, or orientation and invite shortcut solutions or destructive feature drift.
Independent nonlinear visualization fits can make unrelated 2D layouts appear qualitatively different even without meaningful information loss.
Representations may rotate, rescale, or redistribute information under fine-tuning; CKA and selected-neuron correlations can call this erasure even when another readout recovers the variable.
Symbolic regression can select a visually suggestive subterm inside an otherwise spurious expression, especially when candidates and rankings are not evaluated on a fresh law-discovery split.
MAPE can explode near small target magnitudes and Pearson correlation can remain high under severe scale miscalibration, as illustrated by Uranus.
A fixed global probe fails when the relevant physical gradient rotates substantially over state space, while a time-dependent probe may solve the task rather than measure encoding.
The claimed error bound can fail for highly nonlinear decoders even when end-to-end next-state error is small, because a large Taylor remainder can cancel the linear term.
A representative or well-initialized adaptation procedure may preserve physics; the paper's corruption claim need not transfer beyond random-head/narrow-data full fine-tuning.
reusable_insights: Freeze the backbone when the question is what pretraining already encoded, and report adaptation as a distinct capability-acquisition experiment.
Use a capacity ladder—raw inputs, fixed linear, time-dependent linear, nonlinear frozen, last-layer, and full fine-tuning—to separate accessibility from supervised relearning.
Pair representation probes with OOD parameter shifts so a readout must extrapolate beyond the probe-training regime.
Before calling a decoded observable a learned law, test whether the target is directly computable from model inputs and require the corresponding analytic raw-input positive control to succeed.
Separate predictive fidelity, linear accessibility, causal use, and symbolic law recovery; success on one is not evidence for all four.
Use nested splits for activation-layer selection, probe fitting, symbolic-expression selection, and final physical OOD evaluation.
When comparing representation geometry before and after tuning, fit one aligned reducer or use invariant quantitative tests rather than independent nonlinear maps.
To establish erasure, search the full subspace for retained information and perform a rescue/intervention, not only maximum correlations among the most-modified neurons.
Audit theoretical probes against the implemented target: an update-level theorem does not validate a state-level readout without explicitly supplying the current state.
Bound every Taylor remainder used to convert end-to-end predictor error into latent linearity; otherwise present the relation as a heuristic.
Include representative-data fine-tuning and linear-probe-then-fine-tune controls before generalizing corruption from random-head adaptation.
Report symbolic formula accuracy, dimensional consistency, seed stability, and recovery of every required variable—not merely a recognizable subterm.
open_questions: Does PhyIP still recover energy after removing pressure or other target-sufficient channels from the input and latent representation?
Why does the TRL raw-input linear baseline fail when the target is exactly the spatial integral of 1.5P?
Can a corrected theorem relate end-to-end SSL error to a fixed linear readout while explicitly controlling decoder curvature and the latent distribution?
Does a probe trained on Delta s, rather than s(t+1), reproduce the empirical results predicted by the stated theory?
How much of the RSG and orbital performance remains after choosing the layer on an ID validation split and evaluating once on untouched OOD systems?
Can causal interventions along the decoded energy or force directions alter next-state predictions in the physically expected way?
Does information about radius and speed truly disappear after fine-tuning, or move into a rotated/distributed subspace recoverable by a fresh controlled probe?
Would representative mass/radius fine-tuning, LP-FT, weight decay, or feature-preserving regularization avoid the reported collapse?
Are the fluid results stable across seeds, simulator resolutions, aggregation choices, and alternative error metrics with confidence intervals over independent trajectories?
Can symbolic regression recover m1*m2/r^2, rather than only a 1/r^2 subterm, on a held-out grid varying both masses and radius?
What explains good next-state error but poor linear energy decoding for RSG FNO/TFNO?
How should probe capacity be calibrated for physical functionals whose gradients legitimately rotate across the state manifold?

competitive_landscape.title: What Has a Foundation Model Found? Using Inductive Bias to Probe for World Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct benchmark and opposing evaluation method
competitive_landscape.difference: Vafa et al. define an inductive-bias probe by adapting a pretrained model to small synthetic tasks and interpreting OOD behavior as evidence about its preferred world model. PhyIP reuses their orbital setup but argues that adaptation changes the object being measured, replacing it with frozen linear decoding plus symbolic regression; this difference is exactly what the orbital experiment tests.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICML 2025 / PMLR 267, pp. 60727-60747; conference_date=2025-07-13--2025-07-19; proceedings publication_date=2025-10-06

competitive_landscape.title: From Kepler to Newton: Inductive Biases Guide Learned World Models in Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Liu et al. change training and architecture—continuous regression, context noise, and temporal locality—and obtain nearly exact force representations (R2 about 0.999), distinguishing Keplerian from Newtonian strategies. PhyIP keeps a standard pretrained model fixed and asks what approximate physics is already linearly accessible, so it addresses evaluation corruption rather than which inductive biases cause acquisition.

competitive_landscape.title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution
competitive_landscape.difference: Kumar et al. prove and test conditional OOD feature distortion across ten vision distribution shifts and show LP-FT mitigates it, with average FT versus LP OOD accuracy 59% versus 66% and LP-FT 68.9%. PhyIP transfers the warning to physical world-model diagnosis and adds CKA/variable analyses, but does not test Kumar et al.'s LP-FT remedy or a representative adaptation set.

competitive_landscape.title: Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: Hewitt and Liang quantify selectivity with randomized control tasks that expose a probe's capacity to memorize. PhyIP instead restricts the probe to be fixed and linear and uses raw/time-dependent/MLP/adaptation baselines; it does not include an analogous randomized control-label selectivity test.
competitive_landscape.source_version: EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019 official proceedings record; publication_date=2019-11; DOI 10.18653/v1/D19-1275

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent Linear Representations in World Models of Self-Supervised Sequence Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Nanda et al. find a linear Othello board representation and causally steer model behavior with activation vectors, tying accessibility to use in a discrete game. PhyIP extends frozen linear probing to continuous physical observables and OOD laws, but supplies no comparable activation intervention showing that decoded energy or force is causally used.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first non-invasive physical probing framework that treats frozen neural dynamics models as measurement instruments, derives an SSL-error/curvature bound for fixed linear decoding, recovers internal-energy and inverse-square laws OOD, and mechanistically shows that invasive adaptation overwrites latent physics.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper combines frozen linear probes, 39 fluid OOD regimes, 50 orbital OOD tests, symbolic regression, layer sweeps, CKA, parameter-change maps, neuron-variable correlations, and a solar-system appendix. Its clearest empirical contrast is frozen versus full-tuned orbital performance (rho 0.91 versus 0.05) and the supernova false-positive control (frozen rho at most 0.21 versus full FT 0.71).
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The evaluation-design message and cross-domain capacity ladder are useful, and the negative supernova result is unusually informative. The strongest novelty is methodological synthesis rather than a validated theorem or definitive proof of erasure: the bound has an uncontrolled decoder remainder and target mismatch, block selection leaks OOD data, fluid targets can be input-derived, geometry plots are independently fitted, and the symbolic result recovers only a partial 1/r^2 term. The evidence supports 'narrow-data fine-tuning can obscure a frozen linear code' more strongly than 'adaptation corrupts latent physics' in general.

reviewer_notes: All 21 extracted pages were read, including Appendices A-H. PDF pages 5, 7, 8, 15, 16, and 19-21 were directly inspected to resolve Tables 1-4, the error-bound derivation, PaCMAP procedure, solar results, resolution metadata, and symbolic formulas. The current arXiv record is v1 dated 2026-02-12. Five competitors were checked on official arXiv, PMLR, and ACL primary records on 2026-08-23, with current versions and source/publication dates recorded. The review preserves negative/null outcomes (SN failure, FNO/TFNO low-error non-decoding, Venus/Uranus/Neptune weaknesses) and distinguishes author statements from reviewer inference. This is a primary full-text pass, not independent replication.
